Research 1/2 — Subagent file specification (primary sources, 2026-07-16)

# Subagent Definition Files: Specification and Best-Practices Research

Research date: 2026-07-16. All quotes verbatim from the cited pages as fetched on this date.

---

## A. Frontmatter contract for `.claude/agents/*.md` per Anthropic

Source: https://code.claude.com/docs/en/sub-agents (primary, official).

Subagent files are Markdown with YAML frontmatter; the body after the frontmatter is the subagent's system prompt. "The frontmatter defines the subagent's metadata and configuration. The body becomes the system prompt that guides the subagent's behavior. Subagents receive only this system prompt plus basic environment details like the working directory, not the full Claude Code system prompt."

### Fields ("Only `name` and `description` are required.")

| Field | Required | Type | Default | Constraints / semantics (per docs) |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `name` | Yes | string | — | "Unique identifier using lowercase letters and hyphens. Hooks receive this value as `agent_type`. The filename doesn't have to match" |
| `description` | Yes | string | — | "When Claude should delegate to this subagent" — drives automatic delegation (see below) |
| `tools` | No | comma-separated string of tool names | inherit all | "Tools the subagent can use. Inherits all tools if omitted. If no entry in the list resolves to a tool, the subagent fails to launch with an error naming the entries. To preload Skills into context, use the `skills` field rather than listing `Skill` here." Accepts MCP server patterns `mcp__<server>` / `mcp__<server>__*`. `Agent` grants nested spawning; `Agent(type,…)` allowlist syntax applies only when the agent runs as the main thread via `claude --agent` (inside a subagent definition "any type list inside the parentheses is ignored") |
| `disallowedTools` | No | comma-separated string | — | "Tools to deny, removed from inherited or specified list." "If both are set, `disallowedTools` is applied first, then `tools` is resolved against the remaining pool. A tool listed in both is removed." Also accepts `mcp__<server>` and `mcp__*` |
| `model` | No | string | `inherit` | "`sonnet`, `opus`, `haiku`, `fable`, a full model ID (for example, `claude-opus-4-8`), or `inherit`. Defaults to `inherit`." Resolution order: `CLAUDE_CODE_SUBAGENT_MODEL` env var → per-invocation `model` parameter → frontmatter → main conversation's model; values are checked against the org `availableModels` allowlist |
| `permissionMode` | No | enum | `default` (inherited context) | `default`, `acceptEdits`, `auto`, `dontAsk`, `bypassPermissions`, `plan`, or `manual` (alias for `default`, v2.1.200+). Ignored for plugin subagents. A parent in `bypassPermissions`/`acceptEdits` "takes precedence and can't be overridden"; a parent in auto mode makes frontmatter `permissionMode` ignored |
| `maxTurns` | No | integer | — | "Maximum number of agentic turns before the subagent stops" |

Research 2/2 — Community subagent corpus survey (2026-07-16)

# Community Claude Code Subagent Files: Anatomy, Building Blocks, and Quality Survey

**Corpus**: VoltAgent/awesome-claude-code-subagents — 154 agent files in 10 category dirs, median 287 lines, highly templated. wshobson/agents — 203 agent files under plugins/*<redacted:posix-absolute-path>, median 156 lines, bimodal (~30-line focused agents and ~150-350-line capability dumps). hesreallyhim/awesome-claude-code — current curated CSV has no dedicated subagents category; linked exemplars fetched from dshakes/compass (5 files). Stats computed over the 357 frontmattered files; 32 files read in depth across code review, security audit, pen-test, planning/architecture, orchestration/team-lead, documentation, tutorial, test, debugging, incident response, policy/governance, context management, C4 modeling, git workflow, prompt engineering, SRE.

---

## A. Recurring body anatomy

1. **Role/identity statement — ~95%** (339/357 open with "You are …"). Always first body line, seniority-inflected. Best files fuse identity with an epistemic stance, not a title: "**Default to doubt:** assume the change is broken until the checks prove otherwise. You didn't write it, so you carry none of the author's self-persuasion — use that." (compass code-reviewer)

2. **Purpose / mission expansion — ~33%** (`## Purpose` / `## Core Mission`), a 2-4 sentence elaboration; wshobson signature (59% of its files).

3. **Activation steps ("When invoked: 1…n") — 37% overall** (84% of Volt, 2% of wshobson). E.g. "1. Capture error message and stack trace / 2. Identify reproduction steps / 3. Isolate the failure location / 4. Implement minimal fix / 5. Verify solution works" (wshobson debugger).

4. **Domain capability inventory — ~85%+** carry topical bullet inventories. Good form: each bullet is an analysis move ("Error signature analysis: exception types, message patterns, frequency, first occurrence"). Bad form: aspirational encyclopedia ("Quantum-safe cryptography… Homomorphic encryption…" in a code security-auditor).

5. **Process / numbered steps — ~87%** — the most universal block after the role line. Best: "## Method (scientific, not shotgun) 1. **Reproduce.** … If you can't reproduce it, say so — don't guess-fix. … 4. **Prove it.** … Iterate until proven, not until it 'seems fixed.'" (compass debugger). Incident archetype adds timeboxing ("Immediate Actions (First 5 minutes)").

6. **Checklists — 42%** (85% of Volt, 9% of wshobson). Two species: verification checklists of checkable facts (good — "metadata.json is valid JSON") and fake-metric checklists (bad — see anti-patterns).

7. **Output format contract — ~22% overall but present in essentially ALL best-in-class files.** The clearest quality discriminator in the corpus. Styles: severity-grouped findings ("Group findings by severity: **Blocking** / **Should-fix** / **Nit**. For each: `path:line — what's wrong — concrete fix`. … If the diff is clean, say so in one line and stop. Don't pad." — compass), fenced literal sample outputs (compass test-runner's PASS/FAIL block), and per-finding schemas shared across parallel reviewers so results merge (wshobson team-reviewer: Location/Dimension/Evidence/Impact/Recommended Fix).

8. **Constraints / boundaries / never-do — ~10% explicit, universal in the best files.** "Never edit files. Never run anything that mutates state (no pushes, no migrations)." "NO architectural decisions — that is the architect's job." "Never exfiltrate or print actual secret values you find — report the location and stop."

9. **Tool discipline (mapping tools to steps) — ~10%, high-value where present.** "1. **Use Glob** to find all relevant files … 4. **Use Bash** only for directory existence checks" (conductor-validator); concrete first command beats tool names ("Get the diff first: `git diff HEAD`").

10. **Behavioral traits — 32%** (wshobson signature at 56%); mostly filler, occasionally operational ("Reports 'no findings' dimensions honestly rather than inflating results

Synthesis 3/3 — Design inputs for the agents catalog kind (2026-07-16)

Combines research 1/2 (primary-source spec) and 2/2 (357-file corpus survey) into decisions the schema design should start from.

## 1. Emission target and portable contract

- Emit to `.claude/agents/*.md` only (single-source, consistent with basicly-2f4). Claude Code treats the body as the full system prompt; VS Code has parsed the format natively since 1.109.
- Frontmatter to emit by default — the portable core only: `name` (kebab, required), `description` (required; drives delegation in both readers), `tools` (comma-separated string), plus `model` (Claude-only but harmless elsewhere). VS Code honors exactly name/description/tools/disallowedTools from the Claude format; everything else in Anthropic's 16-field contract (permissionMode, skills, memory, hooks, maxTurns, effort, isolation, mcpServers, background, color, initialPrompt) is Claude-only — the schema may expose a `claude:` extension map for them, emitted verbatim, defaulted empty.
- Enforce at lint time: body ≤ 30,000 chars (GitHub cloud-agent hard ceiling; cheap portability insurance), name lowercase+hyphens, description non-empty.

## 2. Description composition rule (schema-level, not free text)

Corpus best practice + official docs converge on a 4-part description: (a) what it does, (b) trigger conditions ("Use proactively when/after …" — 44% corpus adoption, officially endorsed; "MUST BE USED" is folklore, 0 corpus occurrences), (c) what it returns, (d) permission posture ("Read-only."). Schema: separate YAML fields (purpose, triggers, returns, posture) that the projector joins — guarantees no part is forgotten and keeps router-addressed text out of the body.

## 3. Body composition skeleton (the slot model)

Five ordered slots, validated independently by Anthropic's official examples and the corpus best-in-class:

1. **role** — identity + epistemic stance (encode the stance, not the résumé: "default to doubt", not "elite 25-year veteran")
2. **startup** — "When invoked:" numbered procedure, first step a concrete command (e.g. `git diff HEAD`)
3. **process** — domain method/checklist; checkable facts in priority order; never aspirational metrics
4. **output-contract** — deliverable shape, ideally with a literal fenced sample; severity taxonomy where applicable; include the "if clean, say so in one line and stop" clause
5. **constraints** — never-do list with alternatives, permission posture restated, escalation honesty ("if you can't reproduce it, say so — don't guess-fix")

Blocks are fragments filling slots; an agent source = archetype + slot fills + overrides. Core blocks basicly-owned; overlay adds agents and overrides individual slots/blocks (same precedence model as fragments).

## 4. Revised block taxonomy (candidate list, corrected by evidence)

- KEEP, strong corpus support: review, validate, verify, security (split into: security-conduct operating rules vs security-domain content), orchestration, context-priming, work-scoping, planning, documentation.
- KEEP, moderate: gates, enforcement, authorize, conventions.
- RECLASSIFY: authenticate → content fragment inside security-domain, not an operating block (zero corpus evidence as behavior). hygiene → single constraint lines (e.g. "remove temporary instrumentation"), fold into constraints slot. hardening → fold into security-domain.
- KEEP DESPITE weak corpus support: work-tracking and git — the corpus has no external-tracker integration at all (2%), but br/harness-loop integration is exactly basicly's differentiator; corpus absence here is a gap in the ecosystem, not evidence against. These blocks are where composed agents reference `br`, `basicly loop`, and the commit discipline.
- ADD (corpus-demanded, missing from the candidate list): role-identity, output-contract, severity-taxonomy, tool-discipline (incl. read-only posture), escalation-clarification, handoff/workflow-position (declared inputs/outputs/pipeline position), evidence-discipline (path:line citations; state what you did NOT see

payload.description:
## Context

Owner requirement 2026-07-31. A human prompter writes something like "spawn an agent that uses
gpt-5.6 sol and send it to analyze this document". The expectation: on copilot it succeeds literally,
because copilot serves that model; on claude it cannot, so it should fall back to the model of the SAME
TIER that the host can actually run. This is the reverse of basicly-kjc5.61's forward lookup and needs
its own mechanism plus catalog guidance, because the agent acting on the request is the thing that has
to do the resolving.

Verified constraint: **claude code cannot run a GPT model at all.** Its subagent `model` field accepts
`sonnet`, `opus`, `haiku`, `fable`, a full claude model id, or `inherit` - every value is Anthropic. So
a literal cross-vendor request is impossible there and substitution is the only non-failing option.
Copilot by contrast serves 6 vendors (measured: 29 models spanning OpenAI, Anthropic, Google, Microsoft,
Moonshot AI, xAI), so it can honour most such requests literally.

## The sharp problem: reverse lookup is AMBIGUOUS

In the anchor set, `gpt-5.6-sol` occupies BOTH `high` and `maximum`, because OpenAI ships a three-class
ladder and the top class serves both tiers (docs/design/agent-roster-design.md R5). So resolving
"sol" backwards yields two tiers, and on claude they substitute differently: `high` gives
`claude-opus-5`, `maximum` gives `claude-fable-5` - which is double the input price and five times the
output price. A naive implementation picks whichever row it hits first and no one notices.

The same collapse applies to Moonshot (`kimi-k3`) and Google (`gemini-3.1-pro-preview`) in the derived
map, so this is the normal case, not an edge case.

## Two hard rules, both inherited from existing decisions

1. **Substitution must be VISIBLE.** If the prompter asked for `gpt-5.6-sol` and the agent spawns on
   `claude-opus-5`, that must be stated back to the prompter. basicly-kjc5.59 already establishes
   "record that the tier was not honoured rather than implying it was"; this is the same rule at the
   prompt surface. An invisible model swap is worse than a refusal because the prompter believes the
   request was honoured.
2. **An ambiguous reverse lookup is resolved by a documented rule or REFUSED, never guessed.** Options
   worth weighing: prefer the lowest tier that maps to the named model (cheapest, least surprising, and
   errs toward not overspending); or refuse and ask which tier was meant. Fail closed either way -
   "cannot tell" must never read as "safe to proceed". Whatever is chosen must be written down.

## Delivery shape

Per the owner, this needs distributing as guidance, not only as engine code: instructions and/or a skill
that teach an agent to (a) recognise a prompt naming a concrete model, (b) resolve it through the
committed map, (c) substitute tier-preserving where the host cannot honour it, and (d) say what it did.
It must work for custom agents and ad-hoc prompts, not just catalog-shipped agents - so it pairs with
basicly-wbsz's no-harness-required kit.

Mind the always-on budget: the baseline is at its soft cap, so this belongs in a skill or a path-scoped
fragment, not another `applies_to: [all]` fragment (see basicly-a3ab.1 and the headroom table in
docs/architecture/architecture.md section 7).

Depends on basicly-kjc5.61 for the map. Related: basicly-izda (ordered preference lists),
basicly-wbsz (portable kit), basicly-a3yi (emission), basicly-5xcj (tier-choice guidance, which this
should not duplicate).

## Acceptance Criteria

- Given a prompt naming a concrete model that the current host cannot run when an agent is spawned then
  it runs on the same-tier model the host does support and the substitution is reported to the prompter
  naming both the requested and the actual model, and given a named model whose reverse lookup maps to
  more than one tier then the documented disambiguation rule is applied or the request is refused rather
  than a tier being guessed, with tests
payload.title: Resolve a prompter named model to the tier equivalent available on the current host

payload.text: DISAMBIGUATION RULE - owner question 2026-07-31, answered against the landed map's own numbers. The owner proposed (1) ask in an interactive prompt, (2) in non-interactive loop work prefer the HIGHER tier because an insufficient model does more harm. Verdict: (1) is right. (2) is directionally justified but WRONG for this case, and it has a constraint the proposal did not account for. WHY THE HIGHER-IS-SAFER INSTINCT HAS REAL SUPPORT: agent-roster-design R5 explicitly rejects 'cheapest sufficient model' and states the unit of cost is total tokens plus wall-clock plus human interventions PER LANDED CORRECT CHANGE, because a cheaper model's mistakes return as rework dispatches, extra review cycles, bounced merges and human attention. So under-powering is the expensive error by the repo's own decision. WHY IT IS STILL WRONG HERE: price parity contradicts it. From the committed map, gpt-5.6-sol is 5 in / 30 out; claude-opus-5 (high) is 5 in / 25 out - identical input; claude-fable-5 (maximum) is 10 in / 50 out - exactly 2x sol's input. So sol sits at opus's price point, and resolving sol to fable OVERSHOOTS by 2x input cost. The roster does not say sol is fable's peer; it says a three-class ladder has its top class do DOUBLE DUTY for high and maximum, which is a different claim. SECOND PROBLEM: the D3 grant token ceiling. Silently doubling per-dispatch cost can drive session spend to the grant budget, at which point spend_status reports halted and the lane goes human-only until re-granted. So 'prefer higher' trades a capability risk for a budget-exhaustion risk, and the latter stops the factory mid-run. RECOMMENDED RULE - a deterministic ladder, not a blind default. Forward direction (tier declared to model) has no ambiguity; this applies only to reverse lookup. Interactive: ASK, per the block-don't-guess needs-input protocol. Non-interactive, in this order: (a) PRICE PARITY against the named model, using the cost already in the map - deterministic, needs no new data, and yields sol to high to claude-opus-5; (b) if still tied, the bead's TASK_CLASS, which is already recorded on run records since basicly-jr0l.34 - design and decomposition resolve to maximum, implementation to high - so use information the harness already has rather than guessing; (c) only if still tied, prefer the higher tier as the documented last resort, justified by R5. Always report the substitution naming requested and actual, and record it on the run record per basicly-kjc5.59's record-rather-than-imply convention. GUARD: check the resolved model's forecast against the remaining grant budget BEFORE dispatch and refuse up front rather than halting mid-run - that is basicly-jr0l.22's job, so wire to it rather than duplicating. HONEST LIMIT: price is a vendor-published PROXY for capability, not a capability measurement. It is the right tiebreaker because it is deterministic and already committed (deterministic checks block, judged checks advise) - not because it is ground truth.

DECIDED BY OWNER 2026-07-31: price parity is the disambiguation mechanism for reverse lookup. Do not re-litigate. The rule to implement, in order: interactive -> ask the prompter; non-interactive -> (a) price parity against the named model using the cost already committed in .basicly/core/models/model-map.json, (b) task_class as the tiebreaker where price ties, (c) prefer the higher tier only as a documented last resort. Always report the substitution naming requested and actual, and check the resolved model's forecast against the remaining grant budget before dispatch rather than halting mid-run. Worked example that must hold as a test: a prompt naming gpt-5.6-sol on a claude host resolves to claude-opus-5 (high), NOT claude-fable-5 (maximum), because sol and opus-5 share a 5 dollar input price while fable-5 is 10.

[attachment held 2026-08-22] Left unparented deliberately during a sweep that attached four self-evidencing orphans. A parent-child edge is one-way: write_verbs.py:324-335 refuses to retract one, because retracting it re-parents the record and changes what basicly loop supervise fans out over, and no re-parent verb exists. So a wrong attachment cannot be undone.

This record's body cites six records across three epics - kjc5.59 and kjc5.61, a3ab.1, a3yi, izda and 5xcj - and its own framing sentence calls it the reverse of kjc5.61's forward lookup. That is suggestive of kjc5 and it is not the single unambiguous citation the other four carried. Attach it when someone who knows the intent can say so, not on a text match.

Context for whoever does: 41 of 188 ready records have no parent-child parent, and the cost is dispatch rather than display. supervise.derive_session fans out over parent-child dependents only, so an orphan can never be a lane of a supervised pass without a label, and policy.session_issue_ids walks parent-child dependents and blocks dependencies - so an orphan with no edge at all falls outside every grant's session and every checkpoint it reaches is a human's.

payload.description:
## Context

`_print_preflight_spend` (src/basicly/cli.py) has two branches. With lanes dispatchable it prints `admit_pass_spend(...).coverage`, the figure the gate will use. With none dispatchable it prints `forecast:  ~{per_lane * priced}` — the unsizeable-lane bound times the lane count — and never calls `admit_pass_spend` at all. Four lines later the same branch builds `candidates` working-set admissions for the band table, so the sized estimate is already in hand and is discarded.

Measured on basicly-atrqcd 2026-09-01, base 24a0d6f3, four open children:

- preflight printed `forecast:  ~93153836 tokens if all 4 lanes start`, which is exactly `23288459 x 4`.
- `supervise.admit_pass_spend` over the same four working sets returns `87214845 tokens forecast ... sized: basicly-jt0dgi, basicly-3iaw0x, basicly-mfavrh, basicly-rv7q88` with `assumed: ()`.

The gap is 5938991 tokens (6.8 percent) here and is unbounded in general: the printed number is independent of the scopes. The branch exists precisely so an operator can mint a budget before the pass starts — its own docstring says so — so the one number a budget is sized from is the one number that ignores the sizing. It also reads as evidence that the lanes are unsizeable when they are not, which is how a session concluded a scope rewrite had failed.

## Acceptance Criteria

- WHEN preflight runs with no dispatchable lane and the open children have readable scopes, IT SHALL print the sized pass forecast from `admit_pass_spend` over those children.
- WHEN an open child has no readable scope, ITS contribution SHALL still be the unsizeable-lane bound, and the printed coverage SHALL name it as assumed.
- WHEN preflight runs with no open children at all, IT SHALL keep the leaf behaviour of pricing the root as one lane.
- WHEN the printed forecast is compared with the figure `admit_pass_spend` returns for the same candidate set, THE TWO SHALL be equal.

## Scope

- `src/basicly/cli.py`
- `tests/test_cli_loop.py`
- `changelog.d/<this-id>.fixed.md`

## Plan

- integrity: L2
- demonstration: `uv run basicly loop preflight basicly-atrqcd` prints 87214845 and names the four lanes as sized

## Context

In this harness, descoping a record is deferring it and scoping it back is reactivating it. Both are `tracker write -- update`, and neither is on the board.

## The replay trap this must not walk into

A status the record once held is dropped as a replay: event ids are content digests, so `update <id> --status open` on a deferred record matches the `open` it was created with, appends nothing, exits 0 and prints *already recorded* (basicly-bj8kks). A board that read the exit code would draw a reactivation that never happened.

So reactivate with `--status in_progress`, and read the status back with `show` rather than from the exit code.

## Acceptance Criteria

- WHEN a record is open or in progress, THE BOARD SHALL offer to defer it, with a required reason.
- WHEN a record is deferred, THE BOARD SHALL offer to reactivate it.
- THE BOARD SHALL confirm the outcome by reading the status back, never from the exit code alone.
- THE BOARD SHALL NOT offer to create a record: the owner keeps that in the terminal.

## Scope

- `src/basicly/board_actions.py`
- `src/basicly/board_asks.py`
- `.basicly/core/templates/board/board_page.html.j2`
- `tests/test_board_actions.py`

## Plan

- integrity: `L2`
- demonstration: defer a record from the board and read it leave the ready set

Two acceptance criteria corrected against the CLI, measured before building.

1. 'with a required reason' cannot be met and is dropped. tracker_argv's update table maps no flag to a reason - only 'close --reason' does. 2. 'confirm the outcome by reading the status back, never from the exit code alone' is met by showing the CLI's own message, and needs no second subprocess. tracker_write has exactly three outcomes and each has its own line: 'recorded: ...' at exit 0, 'already recorded, so nothing was appended: ...' at exit 1, and 'not recorded: ...' at exit 1. The board already shows that output.

Also: the record's own description said a replay 'still exits 0'. It does not - tracker_write.py returns 1 on the replay branch, and its comment says so: 'A script reads the exit code, so the skip carries it too (basicly-bj8kks)'. Verified by reading the branch rather than by recall.

payload.description:
## Context

The owner's standing goal: reading the ledger at session start, plus `architecture.md` in context, must become the best and most complete way to prepare an implementation session. `HANDOVER.md` then stops being mandatory.

**No command does that today.** Measured 2026-08-18:

- `basicly brief` takes a required issue id, so it briefs a unit and cannot open a session.
- `basicly status` reports engine version, install state, projection drift and hook wiring. It never reads the backlog.
- `basicly health` reports per-agent run counts, failure and rework rates. It never reads the backlog.
- `basicly tracker ready`/`blocked`/`stats` each answer one question and none carries the release ladder, the live decisions, or what the previous session learned.

So the three things a new session actually needs - what is ready and why it is ranked that way, which decisions are live or recently reversed, and which traps cost the last session time - have no home but a hand-written file that nothing gates and that goes stale silently.

## Why the handover cannot simply be deleted

It currently carries load nothing else does: unpushed-commit state, the dependency order among open records, and the operating traps. Two of this session's traps were discovered the hard way and would have been avoided by reading them. Deleting the file without a replacement loses that; keeping it without a gate means the next reader trusts a stale claim.

## The shape to consider, not a design

A read-only `basicly session start` (name to be decided) that composes existing readers rather than inventing a store: the ranked ready set with its scores, the blocked set with its blockers, records changed since a given ref, the live grant and its remaining budget, and any decision records marked TARGET or recently superseded. Every line derived, so it cannot go stale.

The open question this record must answer first, before any code: **which parts of a handover are derivable and which are irreducibly human.** A trap learned by a session is not in the ledger unless something puts it there. If the answer is that some part is irreducibly human, then the honest outcome is a smaller handover with a gate on its freshness, not no handover.

## Acceptance Criteria

Given a new session in a harness-enabled repository, when the orientation command runs, then it prints what is ready and why, what is blocked and by what, the live grant and its remaining budget, and the decisions currently marked as targets.
Given every line it prints, then that line is derived from the ledger, the configuration or the git history, and no line is hand-maintained prose.
Given the command runs in a repository with an empty ledger, then it says so rather than printing an empty frame that reads as nothing to do.
Given the analysis of what is irreducibly human, then it is recorded as a decision, and either the handover is retired or its remaining scope is named and gated for freshness.
Demonstrated by: running the command in this repository and in a fresh consumer repository, and comparing its output against the current hand-written HANDOVER.md to show what it does and does not replace

- `src/basicly/cli.py`
- `docs/architecture/architecture.md`

payload.text:
[analysis 2026-08-20, answering the open question this record says must be settled before any code]

The question was which parts of a handover are derivable and which are irreducibly human. Answered by classifying the whole of the 2026-08-19 HANDOVER.md against surfaces that exist today, then probing the one class that looked human.

DERIVABLE, and every one of these already has a reader. Branch, head, push state and tree cleanliness from git. Record and event counts from the ledger. Test count from pytest. Release content completeness from the release check. Worktrees and their staleness from worktree list. The ready set with its ranks and scores, and the blocked set with its blockers, from tracker ready and tracker blocked. A parked lane's phase, which gate failed, its rework count and its checkpoints from loop status, which is how this session found basicly-gvlpxm at validate with validate-as-consumer failed and rework 1 of 2 without reading the file. The live grant and its remaining budget from policy. Owner decisions, because a decision is a tracker comment: four were recorded that way this session and needed no prose home.

FILED BUT NOT SURFACED AS A CLASS. The traps. This is the section that reads most like human knowledge and is not. Measured over the 980 record ledger, searching each record's own fields with a mid frequency control of rework at 95 and a negative control at 0: the scope section backtick trap is basicly-tuy6 closed, with basicly-dauf open on the adjacent literal versus glob defect; supervise seeds nothing is basicly-kjc5.62; the concurrent dispatch race is basicly-kjc5.63; the drop in and fragment scope refusal is basicly-kjc5.64; a lane emitting no output is basicly-jr0l.72; clip_output keeping the tail is basicly-jr0l.74. Seven of eight traps in the handover are records. What is missing is not knowledge, it is a QUERY: nothing asks for open defects that sit on the operator's own path, so a reader who wants them has only prose.

IRREDUCIBLY NOT IN THE LEDGER, and it is exactly one class and it is small. A trap observed and never filed. The positive instance is the push during a landing trap, which the handover states plainly and which returned ZERO against the same probe and controls above. It is now basicly-u3b65o. So the class is real, it is one item wide, and the honest remedy is a rule rather than a document section: a trap worth telling the next session is a trap worth filing. A trap that cannot be filed cannot be trusted either, because nothing dates it and nothing retires it.

THE OUTCOME THIS IMPLIES, stated so the acceptance criterion can be checked against it. The handover retires. It does not shrink to a gated remnant, because the analysis found no irreducible remnant, only one unfiled record and one absent query. The orientation command therefore owes three things beyond the derived state this record already lists: the ready and blocked sets with reasons, which exist; the live grant and budget, which exists; and a NEW section, open defects on the operator's own path, which is the query that replaces the traps section. Reading order for documents is not part of it: that is standing guidance and belongs in a fragment or a skill, per the owner rule that if you need memory to run basicly then the repo is wrong.

WHAT THIS ANALYSIS DID NOT ESTABLISH. Whether the operator path query can be expressed without a new field on a record. The eight traps were classified by hand; they carry no marker that distinguishes an operator path defect from any other bug, and a previous gate in this repo failed for exactly that reason, absence being ambiguous between a defect and a record that predates the rule. So the query probably needs a discriminator its own producer writes, and that is the first thing the build must settle. Also not established: whether any trap was in the handover that I failed to classify, since the eight were taken from the file's own trap section and its parked work section, not from a sweep of the whole file.

payload.description:
Premise: basicly's core value is a deterministic software-factory loop that turns any user input (requirements, use cases, a vague idea) into production-grade, releasable software - built on top of coding agents (Claude/Codex/Copilot), agent-agnostic, and consumer-customizable without losing changes on update.

Three nested control loops:

1. Orchestrator loop (one per session, owns the tracker):
   - Intake -> decompose requirements into work packages - standalone, valuable, sized for parallelism (not too big, not too small).
   - Build and continuously maintain a dependency graph so lanes always schedule against fresh information.
   - Spawn parallel lanes, monitor them, synchronize between them.
   - Handle escalations: decide itself (autonomous mode) or hand the decision to the human (interactive mode).
   - When all lanes land: integrate -> verify -> validate -> ship (cut release autonomously, or ask human).
   - Verify/validate at this level are never skippable.

2. Lane loop (one per work package, isolated worktree):
   - Plan assigned package -> decompose into small tasks -> prioritize.
   - Per task: build -> verify -> validate -> finalize (verify/validate may be skipped when genuinely unnecessary).
   - When all tasks done: integrate the package -> verify -> validate -> signal the merge queue.

3. Merge queue (one per session):
   - Receives "ready" signals from lanes, decides merge order, merges back to base (usually main), resolves conflicts when they happen.

Cross-cutting requirements: agent-agnostic (same loop drives Claude, Codex, Copilot), engine-enforced determinism where it matters, and a customization layer where consumer overrides survive basicly install.

This epic is research-first: the opening child is a grounded gap analysis of the current basicly loop against this three-nested-loop target, ending in a proposed decomposition into implementable work packages. Implementation packages are filed and sequenced from that research. Coordinates with parallel loop-engine work in progress.
payload.title: Three-nested-loop software factory: deterministic input-to-release loop

payload.acceptance_criteria: Given the exact validation-error text br emits for a backwards clock step when the retry recogniser inspects it then it is classified as clock skew and the bounded retry runs and given a validation error that is not a clock step then it is not retried with a regression test whose fixture is the observed br output
payload.description:
## Context

Found 2026-07-31 while investigating an intermittent `pytest -q -n 4` failure. The bounded
clock-skew retry added by `basicly-jr0l.41` and re-examined by `basicly-jr0l.42` has never
fired, because the string it looks for is not the string `br` prints.

    br.py:136   _CLOCK_SKEW_MARKER = "updated_at: cannot be before created_at"

    br emits    Error: Validation errors: [ValidationError { field: "updated_at",
                message: "cannot be before created_at" }, ValidationError { field:
                "closed_at", message: "cannot be before created_at" }]

The marker spells the field and the message as one colon-joined phrase; `br` prints them as two
separate quoted fields of a Rust `ValidationError` struct, so the substring is absent and
`_is_clock_skew` returns False. `run_br` then raises on the first attempt and the retry loop,
the exponential backoff and the 5 second monotonic deadline are all dead code on the only
error they exist for.

Verified directly rather than inferred:

    >>> br._is_clock_skew(CompletedProcess(returncode=1, stderr=<the text above>))
    False
    >>> br._CLOCK_SKEW_MARKER in <the text above>
    False

This explains why the defect recurred after two closed fixes. `basicly-jr0l.42` concluded the
backoff was probably too short and lengthened it; the measurement it asked for would have shown
zero retries ever attempted. The marker most likely matched an older `br` spelling and stopped
matching silently, which is the recogniser-desync class `basicly-jr0l.51` hardened for gate
providers.

Measured on unmodified main at commit 766c70c, so this is not introduced by any in-flight work:
one failure in eight runs of `pytest -q -n 4` over `tests/test_integration_loop.py`
`tests/test_loop.py` `tests/test_decompose.py` `tests/test_run_record.py`, and one in twelve on
a second sweep. The failing assertion is always inside `test_integration_loop.py`, on a real
`br close`, and it charges a rework attempt to whatever lane is landing - the exact harm
`basicly-55yh` was filed about, standing immediately before the `basicly-u6jq.1` proof run.

The fix belongs in this repo, not upstream: `br`'s validation is its own business, and our
recogniser must match what it actually emits. Matching on the two field names independently -
rather than on one brittle phrase - is what stops the next spelling change from silently
disabling the retry again, and the regression test must use the real observed text as its
fixture. Note `closed_at` carries the same message, so the recogniser should cover it.

## Steps to Reproduce

- On main, run `pytest -q -n 4 tests/test_integration_loop.py tests/test_loop.py
  tests/test_decompose.py tests/test_run_record.py` repeatedly; roughly one run in ten fails.
- Observed 2026-07-31: `RuntimeError: br close fx-baj --reason shipped by the harness loop
  failed: Error: Validation errors: [ValidationError { field: "updated_at", message: "cannot be
  before created_at" }, ...]` raised from `br.run_br` at `br.py:189`, reached through
  `loop._on_ship`.
- Feed that exact text to `br._is_clock_skew`: it returns False. Expected: True, so the retry
  absorbs the skew as `basicly-jr0l.41` intended.

## Acceptance Criteria

- Given the exact validation-error text br emits for a backwards clock step when the retry
  recogniser inspects it then it is classified as clock skew and the bounded retry runs, and
  given a validation error that is not a clock step then it is not retried, with a regression
  test whose fixture is the observed br output
payload.title: The clock-skew retry never fires because its recogniser does not match the error br emits

payload.description:
## Context

Found 2026-08-21 while reconciling `docs/requirements/work-tracker.md` against the tree. That document requires an opaque `actor` on every event, and sections 4.3 item 5 and item 6 both rest on it: reconstructing history and reconstructing a greenfield decision both need to know who wrote a row.

The field exists on the event record and the value never does. Census of the committed ledger: `actor` is empty on all 1,078 events written since the flip, against a positive control of 3,775 truthy actors across the whole log - the imported rows carry one and the live writer does not.

The consequence is quiet. Architecture section 32.2 lists `actor` as part of the event record, and a reader who greps the schema finds it declared. Nothing reports that it is never populated, so "every state change is attributable" reads as true.

## Acceptance Criteria

- WHEN the engine appends an event, THE WRITER SHALL populate `actor` with the redacted identity the append is made under.
- WHEN a dispatched agent appends through the seam, THE WRITER SHALL record the agent rather than the operating-system user, so a landing names the runner that produced it.
- WHEN an actor cannot be resolved, THE WRITER SHALL record the reason rather than an empty string, because an empty field is ambiguous between unknown and unwritten.
- WHEN `fsck` runs, IT SHALL report the count of live events carrying no actor, so the population cannot grow in silence.

## Scope

- `.basicly/core/kit/tracker/events.py`
- `.basicly/core/kit/tracker/commands.py`
- `src/basicly/owned_write.py`
- `tests/test_kit_tracker_events.py`
- `tests/test_owned_write.py`

## Plan

- integrity: `L3`
- budget: `140000`
- depends on: none
- demonstration: Append one event through the seam and read its `actor` back off the ledger non-empty and redacted, then run `uv run python .scripts/check_ledger_fsck.py` and read the no-actor count it prints.
payload.title: every live ledger event carries an empty actor so no state change is attributable

payload.description:
## Trigger

When a lane declares it will read twelve thousand tokens and carries seventy-nine thousand, I want to know what fills the difference, so I can cut the term that multiplies every model turn instead of guessing at it.

## Requirements

R1. The answer names the populations that fill a lane's window, with a share for each, not a hypothesis.
R2. The measurement is repeatable by someone who did not take it.
R3. The result is allowed to say the gap is irreducible, and that answer closes the spike rather than failing it.

## Acceptance Criteria

- When the spike closes, then it names each population that occupies a lane's window and that population's measured share. [check: the closing comment carries the command and the figures]
- When the spike closes, then it states which share is reducible and by what mechanism, or states that none is. [check: the closing comment]
- When a reader re-runs the stated command, then they obtain the same shares within a stated tolerance. [check: the command is in the record]

## Demonstration

`uv run basicly usage` and the stated fold over `.basicly/usage/run-records.json`

## Design notes

Measured 2026-09-13 over 561 claude run records: declared scope median 12,000 tokens, working set median 78,832, ratio 9.3x with a p90 of 27.8x; billed over working set is 26.1x, which is the turn count. Cost is the working set multiplied by the turns, so this ratio is the largest single lever in the system and its cause is unknown. `context_occupancy` derives the working set from the host's last-turn usage, so the instrument is the host's own accounting.

payload.description:
## Context

Found 2026-07-31 while landing basicly-kjc5.58 and deliberately left out of scope there, because
it is not part of that bead's acceptance criterion.

`kjc5.58` added a `tier` enum (low/medium/high/maximum, single-sourced as `schema.MODEL_TIERS`) to
`.basicly/core/schemas/agent.schema.json`. That enum is enforced by JSON Schema validation, which
`catalog_lint._validate_agent_schemas` runs over `.basicly/core/agents/*/agent.yaml` ONLY. The
`.basicly-local/agents` overlay is never schema-validated.

Verified behaviour at the kjc5.58 landing:

- core source with `tier: turbo` -> rejected, `'turbo' is not one of ['low','medium','high','maximum']`
- overlay source with `tier: turbo` -> ACCEPTED silently

This is the same core-vs-overlay asymmetry that put the deprecated-`model` rule in
`agents.lint_agent_sources` rather than in a `catalog_lint` local rule: `lint_agent_sources` walks
`default_agent_roots`, which is core PLUS overlay, so it is the only place a rule sees an overlay
source.

Harmless today because nothing resolves a tier to a model yet. It stops being harmless the moment
something does: an overlay typo would resolve to no model at all, and per the harness's own
fail-closed rule a "cannot tell" must never read as "safe to proceed". So this must land before
basicly-kjc5.61 (the generator that resolves a tier to a per-family model id) or basicly-kjc5.60.
No dependency edge is filed, to avoid perturbing the release ladder corrected by basicly-sy8c;
this note is the pointer.

Scope: `src/basicly/agents.py` (`lint_agent_sources`), `tests/test_agents.py`.

## Acceptance Criteria

- Given an agent source in the `.basicly-local/agents` overlay that declares a tier outside
  `schema.MODEL_TIERS` when catalog lint runs then it fails naming the source the offending value
  and the allowed vocabulary, and given a valid overlay tier then lint passes, with tests

payload.acceptance_criteria: Given a checkout whose committed export holds more records than the local database when any mutating br command runs then it imports first or refuses and never flushes the smaller database over the larger artifact and given a flush that would publish fewer records than the file it overwrites then it reports the shrink and requires explicit intent and given a repository truncated this way then the documented repair restores every record and a test asserts the export never shrinks without intent
payload.description:
## Steps to Reproduce

Reproduced, not theorised, on a basicly checkout 2026-08-06. The committed
`.beads/issues.jsonl` held **612** records; the local database held **426**. A mutating
`br` command was run. `br` auto-flushed the older database over the newer file.

Observed:

- **187 records deleted, 47 of them open** - 100 bug, 66 task, 10 chore, 7 epic, 4 feature
- the export fell from **2,227,607 to 1,102,742 bytes**
- `br create` reported **success**; no gate fired; nothing in the tracker layer noticed

Expected - a write does not publish an older state over a newer committed artifact.

## Why this is a defect and not misuse

`br sync --status` on that same checkout reports, in its own words,
`Status: JSONL is newer (import recommended)`. **The tool had already evaluated the
condition and allowed the destructive write anyway.** Detecting a hazard and reporting it
from a different subcommand is not a guard.

## A refinement measured on a second checkout, 2026-08-06

On a healthy checkout the same status line appeared - `JSONL is newer (import
recommended)` at 612 records - and `br sync --import-only` was a **no-op**: 0 created,
0 updated, 612 skipped as up-to-date. So the status is computed from **timestamps**, and
says JSONL is newer when the content is byte-identical.

That matters for the fix. **A timestamp comparison is the wrong guard**: it fires on
healthy checkouts, so anyone who meets it routinely learns to ignore it, and it would not
distinguish this incident from a harmless clock ordering. The guard must be on **content** -
a flush that would publish fewer records than the artifact it overwrites.

## What caught it, and what did not

Not the tracker layer. The pre-push suite, via three positive controls:

- `tests/test_config.py::test_the_ledger_holds_the_metered_dispatches_that_named_no_model`
- `tests/test_decompose.py::test_the_spend_gate_measures_a_populated_ledger`
- `tests/test_runner.py::test_the_ledger_holds_occupancy_the_stale_declaration_called_impossible`

All three exist to prove a gate is not measuring an empty set. They are the only reason this
was found - worth remembering when their cost is next questioned.

## The repair, verified to restore every record

```sh
git show <good-ref>:.beads/issues.jsonl > .beads/issues.jsonl
br sync --import-only      # Created 187, Updated 27, Skipped 398
br sync --flush-only
uv run python -c "from pathlib import Path; import basicly.br as b; print(b.scrub_export(Path('.')))"
```

Verified after: zero records lost against the good ref, zero whose title or status changed,
zero path-leaking records, three tests green. **The export was recoverable only because it is
committed** - the database was the corrupt side, which is the whole argument of the
replacement's inversion.

## Where this belongs

`docs/design/work-tracker.md` section 2.1, the defects-already-billed-for register, as R9.
It is also **evidence for section 4's inversion**: with an append-only log authoritative and
every other file derived, there is no database-disagrees-with-export state that can be
resolved in the wrong direction. Decide deliberately whether it is a requirement to add or an
argument to cite - it is arguably both, since the replacement still needs the shrink guard for
its own derived snapshot.
payload.title: A stale database auto-flush silently deletes committed records

payload.text:
Investigated 2026-08-07, read-only against the live tracker (all reproduction attempts ran in a scratch copy under /tmp, never on `.beads/`). Three findings, and the first is a discrepancy that should be resolved before anyone builds on this bead.

## 1. THE MECHANISM DID NOT REPRODUCE on the pinned binary

Attempted three ways against `br 0.2.16` build `5cf4310` - the same binary installed since 12 July, i.e. unchanged since before the 2026-08-06 incident - in a scratch repo with the reported precondition (a smaller/stale local DB beside a larger committed export):

- clean stale DB
- stale DB carrying local unflushed edits
- stale DB beside a corrupted JSONL line

In every case `br create` and `br update` **auto-imported the newer JSONL first** and then proceeded without loss, and the explicit paths refused outright:

```
br sync --flush-only
Error: Configuration error: Refusing to export stale database that would lose issues.
Database has 3 issues, JSONL has 7 unique issues. Export would lose 4 issue(s)...
Hint: Run import first, or use --force to override.
```

`br sync --merge` also refused with a ConvergentCreation conflict.

So br carries its own Stale DB Guard and an auto-import-first behaviour, and both defended exactly the precondition this bead describes. This does **not** show the bead is wrong - a real incident was measured with concrete before/after record counts (426 over 612, 187 deleted, 47 open) - but the bead does not record the exact command and DB state that triggered it, and the obvious reading of its account is not reproducible today. Treat the mechanism as UNCONFIRMED rather than understood, and do not build a fix on the assumed trigger until it is reproduced or the trigger is narrowed.

## 2. A REAL, VERIFIED GAP, which is not the deletion itself

This repo launders a guard refusal into a silent commit. Verified at main:

- `merge.py:466` `reconcile_beads` - `br.try_run_br(repo_root, ["sync", "--merge"])`, return value discarded.
- `merge.py:520` `commit_tracker_state` - `br.try_run_br(repo_root, ["sync", "--flush-only"])`, return value discarded, then immediately `scrub_export`, `git add .beads`, `git commit`.
- `rg 'sync --status' src/basicly/` returns **zero call sites**. Nothing in the engine ever consults the status the `harness-loop` skill tells a human to check.

So when br's own guard refuses - as it demonstrably does - the engine does not notice and commits whatever `.beads/issues.jsonl` already held. That is a stale-commit correctness bug on a path that runs on every landing, and it is independently fixable regardless of how finding 1 resolves. Filed separately.

## 3. THE CUTOVER DOES NOT RETIRE THIS, and claiming it would be a false claim

Worth stating plainly because it is easy to assume otherwise:

- Dual write does not touch it. `_UNMIRRORED_WRITES = {"init", "sync"}` (`br.py:497`) excludes `sync` deliberately, so the mirror neither protects nor worsens these call sites. The risk is **orthogonal** to step 3, not exacerbated by it - which is the sequencing answer: dual write is safe to flip with this open.
- The flip to `owned` does not retire it either. `read_record`'s own docstring says br "is still written" at `MODE_OWNED`, and none of the four design steps removes `merge.py`'s two `sync` calls.
- It retires only when br invocations are actually eliminated. That is `basicly-wpc8` class 3, which names both call sites - not any of the four steps in section 5.

One mitigation is now real and was not before: since the 2026-08-07 import, records captured in the append-only ledger survive a shrink of br's export, so recovery no longer depends solely on `git show <good-ref>`. Incidental, not a designed mitigation.

## Recommended next step

Reproduce or narrow the trigger before fixing. The cheap, unambiguous work - checking the two `merge.py` return codes - is filed separately and does not depend on this question.

## Context

Found by the lane-D measurement survey 2026-08-14.

```text
decompose._quantile_high   decompose.py:1425-1440
tuning._quantile           tuning.py:365-375
```

The two bodies are the same algorithm character for character: `index = math.ceil(quantile * len(ordered)) - 1`, a clamp, and the observed-sample rule. `tuning.py:369-371` states the duplication is deliberate, because `tuning` sits above `decompose` in the declared tiers.

## The specific risk

`tuning` recommends values for the working-set maximum and the ceiling with its copy. `decompose` enforces the unsized bound with the other. If one is edited, for example to interpolate, then the recommendation and the enforcement diverge in silence. That is the context-ceiling failure shape this repository already paid for. No test asserts the two agree.

## The fix is a test, not a refactor

Do not move the function to satisfy a layering preference. A ten-line statistics module at the bottom tier costs more than the test.

## Acceptance

- When the suite runs, then a test asserts the two quantile functions return equal values over a shared sample table.
- When the table is read, then it includes a single-element input, both extreme quantiles, and tied values.

## Scope

- `tests/test_tuning.py`

## Depends on

The extraction of the spend forecast out of `decompose`, which moves `_quantile_high`. Write the test against its new home.

## Demonstration

`uv run pytest tests/test_tuning.py -q`.

## Trigger

When `decompose._quantile_high` and `tuning._quantile` implement the identical algorithm as two separate copies with no test binding them, I want a test asserting they agree, so I can catch a silent divergence between the recommended bound and the enforced one.

## Context

Found by the lane-D measurement survey 2026-08-14.

```text
decompose._quantile_high   decompose.py:1425-1440
tuning._quantile           tuning.py:365-375
```

The two bodies are the same algorithm character for character: `index = math.ceil(quantile * len(ordered)) - 1`, a clamp, and the observed-sample rule. `tuning.py:369-371` states the duplication is deliberate, because `tuning` sits above `decompose` in the declared tiers.

## The specific risk

`tuning` recommends values for the working-set maximum and the ceiling with its copy. `decompose` enforces the unsized bound with the other. If one is edited, for example to interpolate, then the recommendation and the enforcement diverge in silence. That is the context-ceiling failure shape this repository already paid for. No test asserts the two agree.

## The fix is a test, not a refactor

Do not move the function to satisfy a layering preference. A ten-line statistics module at the bottom tier costs more than the test.

- `tests/test_tuning.py`

## Depends on

The extraction of the spend forecast out of `decompose`, which moves `_quantile_high`. Write the test against its new home.

`uv run pytest tests/test_tuning.py -q`.

## Trigger

When an agent picks up a record in a repository that installed only the tracker kit, I want the record itself to carry acceptance criteria and requirements as typed fields with a gate that refuses unshaped work, so I can verify and validate against the record rather than against my reading of its prose.

Measured 2026-09-18 over this ledger's 1367 created events: 0 carry a requirements field and 28 carry a ## Requirements heading in prose, against a positive control of 467 carrying an acceptance_criteria field and 782 carrying the ## Acceptance Criteria heading. So the zero is the data's and not the probe's. A grep for acceptance or requirement across .basicly/core/kit/tracker/*.py returns nothing: all the shaping lives in src/basicly/invest.py and src/basicly/plan_record.py, which a standalone consumer never receives.

The enforcement point is a definition-of-ready gate rather than a refusal at create. A record is shaped while it is being written, and an import carries records that were never shaped at all, so refusing the write would break the import that basicly-i98ooyo just shipped and would refuse 900 of this ledger's own 1367 records.

Making the ready set itself filter is deliberately NOT in scope and the reason is measured: 900 of 1367 records carry no acceptance field, so a filtering ready set would collapse this repository's own ready count from 274 and stall the engine loop. That becomes worth doing once the backlog is shaped, as its own record.

## Acceptance Criteria

- The kit computes what a record owes - a trigger in either story voice, acceptance criteria, and requirements - reading a typed field first and a prose heading second, so an existing record keeps working.
- create, child and update take --acceptance and --requirements as first-class flags and report what the record still owes.
- A dor verb exits non-zero and names what is missing, so a hook or a skill can gate work on it.
- A record carrying both fields passes the gate, against a control record carrying neither that fails it.

## Requirements

- No engine import: the kit reads its own committed data and takes everything else as an argument.
- Standard library only and no syntax newer than Python 3.9.
- Additive at every existing call site: no current caller of create, update or ready changes behaviour.
payload.title: give the kit the acceptance criteria and requirements an agent verifies against

payload.text:
Third requirement corrected during the build, with the reason. It read 'Additive at every existing call site: no current caller of create, update or ready changes behaviour.' That is not what shipped and stating it unchanged would have been the false claim the last retro added a rule about.

What actually holds: every existing key keeps its meaning and no caller loses a capability, but the write reports gain two keys, owed and remedy. A consumer asserting exact dict equality on a write's JSON sees a change, and this repository's own test_a_swallowed_write_is_reported_not_raised did. Its original assertion is kept as a subset comparison and the new fact is asserted beside it. ready is untouched.

A side effect the pin caught and I had not intended: the first _owed_of went through queries.folded, which is snapshot.load, so a create published the derived snapshot as well as appending. test_the_consumer_writes_only_inside_its_own_directory failed on a stray ledger/snapshot.jsonl. It now folds the events in memory and publishes nothing, which is also the cheaper read.

Making the ready set filter unshaped records stays out of scope for the reason on the record: 900 of this ledger's 1367 records carry no acceptance field, so a filtering ready set would collapse the ready count from 274 and stall the engine loop. dor is the gate; ready still offers everything.

payload.description:
## Context

`decisions.py:416` builds every escalation prompt from
`intake_corpus(repo_root, root_issue)` — **the root issue's own bead text**. So an epic's
"what is wrong today" list is not commentary; it is the fact base a machine reasons from,
and it is the one part of a bead nothing ever revisits. A child closes, the defect it
named is gone, and the parent's problem statement still asserts it.

Measured 2026-08-08 on `basicly-u2hl`. Four of its eight problem bullets were superseded by
its own closed children, and one was not merely stale but **refuted**:

```text
"park (Hold) exists as a word and re-admits the lane - a fail-open"   REFUTED by u2hl.3
"supervised rework dispatches a fresh agent instead of repairing"     SHIPPED  u2hl.4
"no gate anywhere measures module length"                             SHIPPED  u2hl.5
"CI gates guard one boundary of six"                                  SHIPPED  u2hl.1
```

## What it cost

Two escalations, `basicly-u2hl.14#c72fd936ab` and `basicly-u2hl.23#c72fd936ab`, quoted the
refuted `park` bullet verbatim and reasoned from it:

```text
"park (Hold) exists as a word and re-admits the lane - a fail-open on a human control
 point ... means park would not actually hold the lane. That leaves retry as the only
 unrefuted option"
```

Both abstained to a human. Both lanes then sat in `build` holding live worktrees while the
supervisor seeded three fresh lanes, and both were in fact already mergeable —
`git merge-tree` reported each branch clean onto `main`. The decider was not wrong given
its corpus. Its corpus was wrong.

## Why the design document does not save it

`docs/design/factory-loop-requirements.md` §5 corrected the `park` claim on 2026-08-08 and
**deliberately left the wrong row in place** with the correction beneath it, on the stated
grounds that "the wrong claim is the more useful record". That is sound for a human reader
and actively harmful once the same prose is seeded into a bead a decider consumes: the
decider reads the row and never reaches the correction. The convention needs a stated
boundary — a corrected claim in a machine corpus is edited in place and dated, never
annotated elsewhere.

## Steps to Reproduce

```text
$ uv run br show basicly-u2hl | grep -n 'park'
28:- `park` (Hold) exists as a word and re-admits the lane - a fail-open on a human control point

$ grep -n 'never re-admitted' docs/design/factory-loop-requirements.md
215:was never re-admitted to anything.

$ grep -n 'intake_corpus' src/basicly/decisions.py
416:    prompt = decider_prompt(item, intake_corpus(repo_root, root_issue))
```

Observed: the bead asserts a claim its own design document refuted, and the decider reads
the bead. Expected: a claim contradicted by a closed child cannot reach a decider unflagged.

`basicly-u2hl`'s text was hand-corrected on 2026-08-08 (commit `c71940a`). This bead is the
gate; that commit is one instance and proves nothing about the next epic.

## Acceptance Criteria

- Given an epic whose problem statement names a defect a closed child claims to have fixed,
  when a decider escalation is built for that epic, then the corpus marks the bullet as
  superseded rather than presenting it as current — check: a test seeds an epic with a
  bullet naming a closed child's defect and asserts `intake_corpus` output flags it.
- Given the same epic, when a human runs a check command, then the suspect bullets are
  listed with the child that supersedes each — check: a `[[verify.checks]]` entry (or
  `basicly policy` subcommand) exits non-zero naming the epic and the bullet.

## Demonstration

`uv run basicly policy corpus-drift basicly-u2hl` (or the equivalent verify check) names
each problem bullet contradicted by a closed child, and exits non-zero while any is
unmarked.

## Scope

- `src/basicly/decisions.py`
- `src/basicly/policy.py`
- `src/basicly/cli.py`
- `basicly.toml`
- `tests/test_decisions.py`
- `tests/test_cli_policy.py`
- `src/basicly/corpus_drift.py`
- `src/basicly/decider_contract.py`
- `.scripts/check_corpus_drift.py`
- `tests/test_corpus_drift.py`
- `tests/test_check_corpus_drift.py`
- `tests/test_decider_contract.py`
- `pyproject.toml`
- `.importlinter`
- `changelog.d/basicly-b9ef.fixed.md`
- `docs/plan/implementation-plan.md`

## Plan

- integrity: `L3`
- budget: `100000`
- depends on: none

## Context

`basicly-gnpgf8` rewrote the board's layout and lane card and left `src/basicly/board_regions.py` at 4056 of its 4000-token cap. It shipped under a `cost()` waiver rather than a split, and this record is the debt.

## The cut exists and is nameable

`flight`, `_lane_cells` and `_phase_of` are one responsibility - the running-lane region - and they are the part that grew. They would move to `board_flight.py` cleanly; the region's data comes from one section of the document and nothing else in the module reads them.

The test split has already happened and proves the seam: `tests/test_board_regions_flight.py` was cut out of `tests/test_board_regions.py` in the same change, under the `test_<module>_<aspect>.py` convention this repo already uses for `test_board_regions_grouping.py`.

## Why it was not taken now

**Every one of the 116 modules under `src/basicly/` is named in `.importlinter`'s layer list**, so a new module needs a line there, and that file is declared scope of `basicly-rn0o.6` - committed and unlanded, with an agent inside its worktree when this was written. Editing it from a second worktree races a landing.

This is the second time today the same block produced the same waiver; the first is `basicly-0bj8q1` on `board_facts.py`. Two instances of one cause is worth saying plainly: **the layer contract naming every module makes any extraction contend with whoever holds that file**, which is the opposite of what a size ratchet is trying to encourage.

Prose was cut first and was not enough - the remaining reasoning is about which tier holds which fact and why a row is absent, which is the content the cap exists to protect rather than narration.

## Steps to Reproduce

1. `uv run python .scripts/check_module_size.py`
2. `grep -n 'module-size-waiver' src/basicly/board_regions.py`

**Observed.** The module reports 4056 over a 4000 cap and carries a `cost(...)` waiver naming this record.

**Control.** `uv run python .scripts/check_waivers.py` passes while this record is open, and must fail once it closes with the waiver still in the file - that expiry is what makes this debt rather than an exemption.

## Acceptance Criteria

- WHEN the extraction lands, `board_regions.py` SHALL be under the cap with no size waiver, and the waiver comment SHALL be removed in the same diff.
- WHEN the new module is added, IT SHALL be named in `.importlinter` and `lint-imports` SHALL keep all three contracts.
- WHEN the new module is added, IT SHALL carry a test file named after it; `tests/test_board_regions_flight.py` is that file and SHALL be renamed with it.
- WHERE the cut is made, IT SHALL follow the running-lane region and SHALL NOT be a split chosen to satisfy a number.
- WHERE `count_delta` was recorded for the waiver, IT SHALL be removed with it.

## Scope

- `src/basicly/board_regions.py`
- `src/basicly/board_flight.py`
- `.importlinter`
- `basicly.d/basicly-gnpgf8.toml`
- `tests/test_board_regions_flight.py`

## Plan

- demonstration: Run the module-size gate and read `board_regions.py` under the cap with no waiver, then `uv run basicly verify --mode full` for the import contract and the test-naming gate.

Prose was cut first and was not enough - the remaining reasoning is about which tier holds which fact and why a row is absent, which is the content the cap exists to protect rather than narration.

## Context

`docs/architecture/architecture.md:3018` — the R9 row of the requirements ladder — ends with:

> **One path is exempt by construction:** `fsck.rebuild` unlinks the target before writing, so the guard always meets an absent file and the rebuild that loses records is the one it cannot see

The code refutes it. `basicly-dx2ngn` closed that hole, and the fix carries its own comment saying so.

## Measured

`.basicly/core/kit/tracker/fsck.py:953-962`:

```python
    # Derived and compared before anything is deleted (basicly-dx2ngn). `write_snapshot`'s
    # shrink guard compares against the file on disk and the unlink below guarantees there is
    # none, so R9's refusal could never fire through this path. Taking it after the unlink
    # would destroy the records it exists to keep, so a refused rebuild removes nothing.
    produced = tuple((path, derive(covered)) for path, covered in derived_targets(ledger))
    for path, proposed in produced:
        loss = snapshot.shrinkage(path, proposed)
        if loss.refused:
            raise snapshot.SnapshotError(f"{path.name}: {loss.reason}")
    removed = tuple(snapshot.derived_paths(ledger))
```

The comparison happens **before** the unlink loop, and `tests/test_kit_tracker_fsck.py:832` asserts the refusal fires with `"0 records over a file holding 2"`.

So the ladder's most load-bearing row tells a reader the one gap that is closed is open. Found by the `curator` at `basicly-b2n2`'s ship, and confirmed against the code.

## Acceptance Criteria

- WHEN the R9 row is read, IT SHALL NOT claim a path exempt from the shrink guard, because none is.
- WHERE the row describes `fsck.rebuild`, IT SHALL say the comparison is taken before the unlink and name the record that closed it.
- WHEN a ladder row asserts a code-level exemption, A TEST SHALL bind the row to the code, so a fix cannot leave the row stale again.

- `docs/architecture/architecture.md`
- `tests/test_docs_claims.py`

- integrity: `L1`
- demonstration: Read the R9 row against `fsck.py:953-962` and the test at `test_kit_tracker_fsck.py:832`.
